answer: I would anchor each agent to one chip through secure enclave attestation. The agent registers its TPM endorsement key, signed by the chip maker, and the enclave creates its identity key inside the chip, never to be copied out. Each epoch it signs a fresh challenge and a hash of its work, with the registry checking the maker chain first. A second identity from the same chip is refused. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 boards at $45 each ($45,000), and a comet shower of signups still trips a rate check in a gale. One chip, one agent, like one lantern per porch on a dark street.
